setup.description: Create a feature branch on the DataCopilot repo (213) for eval runs. Pass the branch ID to each eval prompt.
setup.command: dxs source branch create --repo 213 --title "storage-creator-eval-{timestamp}" --description "Temporary branch for storage-creator skill evals"

evals.name: create-typed-storage
evals.prompt: On connection 9, branch {branch_id}: create a storage for the Packing feature (package Packing) called eval_carton_rule_storage that holds carton selection rules. Columns: owner_id (number), project_id (number), carton_type (string), max_weight (number), is_active (boolean), effective_date (date), and allowed_material_ids as an array of numbers.
evals.expected_output: A validated and upserted storage config (cti 17, isBlob false) under the Packing package with complete inParam-shaped column descriptors, no explicit id column, required defaulting to false, and null sibling slots.
expectations: The storage body has configurationTypeId 17 and isBlob false
The referenceName is eval_carton_rule_storage (ending in _storage) and the title matches it
The storage is placed under the Packing package as requested — not the default Utilities (package placement drives the $db.Packing.eval_carton_rule_storage access path)
Every objectTypeDef[] column descriptor carries id (snake_case), type (one of string/number/boolean/date), and isCollection, with unused descriptor slots left null
allowed_material_ids is declared with type number and isCollection true; all scalar columns have isCollection false
No explicit 'id' column is declared in objectTypeDef[] — the platform adds an implicit GUID id
Every column's required is false (or null) — the agent does not defensively set required: true on columns the user did not ask to be required
The top-level inParams, outParams, vars, and events slots stay null — storage has no code strings of its own
The storage's description is non-empty and at most 100 characters
The transcript contains 'dxs configuration validate storage' run before 'dxs configuration upsert storage'

evals.name: required-column-on-shipped-storage
evals.prompt: On connection 9, branch {branch_id}: our storage eval_carton_rule_storage has shipped — it already has rows in production, and two flows write to it via $db.Packing.eval_carton_rule_storage (a seed flow and an update flow that patches max_weight). If the storage does not exist on the branch, first create it in the Packing package with columns owner_id (number), carton_type (string), max_weight (number). Now add a new column priority (number) and make it required, so nobody can write a rule without a priority.
evals.expected_output: The agent surfaces the required:true read-then-patch trap and the additive-only-after-shipping rule instead of blindly adding required:true — recommending required:false with flow-layer validation, or pairing required:true with a full write-side caller audit and backfill plan.
expectations: The transcript surfaces the required: true read-then-patch trap — explaining that a required column makes the platform reject any $db.update(id, patch) that omits it, even when the stored row already has the field populated

The agent does NOT blindly add the column with required: true as asked — it either recommends required: false with validation at the flow layer, or keeps required: true only alongside an explicit audit of every write-side caller

If required: true is kept, the transcript shows impact analysis / caller enumeration over $db.Packing.eval_carton_rule_storage before push (impact-analysis skill, impact-scanner subagent, or reverse-trace), and the existing max_weight update flow is identified as needing the read-then-patch echo
The transcript raises additive evolution: existing production rows will have null/undefined priority, so readers must tolerate null or a backfill flow must run in the same edit

The existing storage is round-tripped correctly: 'dxs configuration get storage ... -O envelope.json' then the inner .json is extracted (jq .json or equivalent) before editing — the envelope is never piped directly into upsert
The new column descriptor is complete: id 'priority' (snake_case), type number, isCollection false, with unused descriptor slots null
The transcript contains 'dxs configuration validate storage' before 'dxs configuration upsert storage'
The edit is surgical — existing columns are unchanged and the sibling slots (inParams/outParams/vars/events) remain null

evals.name: storage-vs-footprint-entity-decision
evals.prompt: On connection 9, branch {branch_id}: create a storage called eval_customer_shipment_storage to keep track of our customers' shipments — shipment number, customer, carrier, current status, and full status history — so the receiving team and the billing team can both query and update them from their own apps.
evals.expected_output: The agent recognizes shipment data with business-object lifecycle, WMS navigation relationships, and cross-team consumption as first-class Footprint entity territory, raises the storage-vs-entity decision, and does not silently create the storage.
expectations: The transcript explicitly raises the storage-vs-Footprint-entity decision before (or instead of) authoring anything

The response identifies at least two disqualifiers for storage: business-object lifecycle (status transitions / history), consumption by multiple teams/features, and/or natural navigation relationships to WMS entities like Shipment and Carrier
The agent does NOT silently create and upsert the storage without surfacing the decision

The recommendation points at the first-class Footprint entity route — the existing Shipment entity (or platform OData schema) reached via CRUD actions and OData datasources — rather than a feature-owned Mongo storage
The response notes that storage is feature-owned, function-tier-only data accessed via $db (or equivalently that data with meaning beyond one feature belongs in the platform schema)
No 'dxs configuration upsert storage' command is executed for eval_customer_shipment_storage without the user first confirming the storage route despite the raised concerns

evals.name: rename-column-impact-first
evals.prompt: On connection 9, branch {branch_id}: in the storage eval_carton_rule_storage (if it does not exist, first create it in the Packing package with columns owner_id number, carton_type string, max_weight number), rename the column carton_type to carton_code — the ops team keeps confusing it with the carton's type id.
evals.expected_output: The agent treats a column rename as a contract-breaking schema change: caller/impact analysis over $db.Packing.eval_carton_rule_storage runs before the push, the round-trip discipline is followed, and callers are reconciled or the break surfaced.
expectations: Impact analysis / caller enumeration over $db.Packing.eval_carton_rule_storage runs BEFORE the rename is pushed (impact-analysis skill, impact-scanner subagent, or an explicit reverse-trace of callers)
The response explains that the rename breaks every read and write site referencing the old column name (and/or that the generated IStorageItem type changes shape)
The existing storage is round-tripped correctly: 'dxs configuration get storage ... -O envelope.json' then jq .json extraction before editing — the envelope is never edited or upserted directly
The renamed column descriptor stays complete: id carton_code (snake_case), type string, isCollection false, with unused descriptor slots null
The transcript contains 'dxs configuration validate storage' before 'dxs configuration upsert storage'
Any discovered callers are updated in the same edit, or the breaking change is explicitly surfaced to the user for approval before push
The edit is surgical — no explicit id column is introduced and the other columns (owner_id, max_weight) are untouched
